customer-attraction/nonterminal-amount-c.scope: Context-only reading, not a task coverage endpoint. For every fixed r≥1, a complete-SPE nonterminal column reaches 2−3/(n+1)→2 with W=OPT.

mathematical_result.terminal_vs_total: The positive-source POOL gives Σ_l q_{αjl}+e_{αj}=p_j(W^α) and one shared AMOUNT yields all-recipient TOTAL≤Σ_{j<m}p_j(B)≤W(B)−p_m(B); this is a total source-pool identity, not a per-target-column cap.
mathematical_result.terminal_cap2: For i_α=m only, c_α≤c_B+1≤2c_B gives Σαλ_{αj}≤2 and terminal removal gives c_α(x)=c_B(x)−1, hence Q_m≤2p_m(B), including zero-profit and m=1 endpoints.
mathematical_result.deep_status: For multi-cut i_α<m, later actions can add or remove several covers, so c_α≤c_B+r and c_α=c_B−1 are unavailable. No general per-column charge converts the one shared AMOUNT into Q_l≤2p_l(B); DEEP-CAP2 remains open even on real same-strategy SPE continuations.
mathematical_result.sharp_lower: Terminal and context fixed-r nonterminal SPE families attain ratio 2−3/(n+1), tending to 2; this rules out any uniform coefficient below 2 while W=OPT, so it is not a half counterexample.
mathematical_result.no_double_spend: POOL retained e, direct/suffix obligations and NET's added-cover compensation all consume the same sender child profit/AMOUNT. They cannot be paid twice, and AMOUNT initialization from OPT/coverage debt remains a separate IC obligation.
